evals.prompt: Fix the typo in the README heading and leave the change for me to commit.
evals.expected_output: Classify this as fast-track work, edit the current branch without creating a branch or commit, and leave the change unstaged and uncommitted.

evals.prompt: Add account deletion across the API, database model, UI, and tests. Keep the Git history easy to review.
evals.expected_output: Classify this as planned work, create a new feat/* branch before editing, validate each cohesive unit, and make multiple small atomic conventional commits containing only explicitly staged task files.

evals.prompt: The feature is already committed on the task branch, but review found a missing authorization check. Fix it without rewriting history.
evals.expected_output: Keep the existing task branch, make the focused authorization fix, validate it, and create a new conventional fix(scope): commit rather than amending the prior commit.

evals.prompt: Add CSV export to the reports page. This repo has no CONTRIBUTING.md.
evals.expected_output: Classify as planned work, offer once to add a CONTRIBUTING.md from references/contributing-template.md filled from the repo's real branches, history and CI; on a yes, commit it on its own as docs; then branch as feat/<slug> from the repo's base branch and make atomic Conventional Commits.

evals.prompt: Implement the new billing endpoint. CONTRIBUTING.md says work branches start from dev, scope is required and lists api, web and db as scopes. I have unrelated uncommitted edits in this checkout I don't want touched.
evals.expected_output: Follow CONTRIBUTING.md over skill defaults: create an isolated sibling worktree on a feat/<slug> branch based on dev without touching the uncommitted edits, and write commits like feat(api): ... using only the listed scopes.

evals.prompt: Commit the staged changes. They contain a bug fix in the parser and an unrelated README rewrite.
evals.expected_output: Do not write one compromise message; split into two atomic commits (a fix(<scope>) commit and a docs commit) by staging explicit paths, each with an imperative subject of at most 72 characters.

evals.prompt: Commit the staged changes: a two-line fix in src/parser.js and a 60,000-line bundle in build/app.min.js that a local build generated.
evals.expected_output: Stop before committing and name build/app.min.js as generated bulk; with confirmation, unstage it, add the exact path to .gitignore in its own chore commit or leave that edit uncommitted and report it, commit only src/parser.js as fix(<scope>), and report the excluded path and reason.

evals.prompt: Commit the account deletion feature. It touches the database model, API route, settings page, and their tests — six files and about 1,200 changed lines in one coherent change.
evals.expected_output: Create one atomic feat(<scope>) commit containing all six files because they implement one functional unit; do not split the files into per-file commits, note the reviewed size in the commit body, and stage explicit paths.

evals.prompt: Stage and commit this refactor: one file loses 700 lines and gains 10 as old branches are removed.
evals.expected_output: Count additions plus deletions, so the file exceeds the 500-line threshold: review the deletion-heavy diff, justify the size in the commit body or handoff, and commit it as refactor(<scope>) rather than treating deletions as small.

evals.prompt: Commit a dependency bump: package.json changes and the lockfile grows by 2,000 lines, all from the same install.
evals.expected_output: Keep the manifest and lockfile in one build(deps) commit because they are one dependency intent; state in the body that the lockfile volume follows the install. Do not split the lockfile into its own commit or treat it as bulk noise.

evals.prompt: Stage and commit a 700-line refactor that renames src/my module.js to src/my module-v2.js; the numstat path contains a space.
evals.expected_output: Use the tab-delimited numstat check so the spaced and renamed path is not dropped, count additions plus deletions, and review and justify the size before committing as refactor(<scope>).

evals.prompt: This repo tracks dist/ and CONTRIBUTING.md requires committing the built bundle with the source. A source change also regenerates dist/app.js by about 3,000 lines.
evals.expected_output: Follow the repository rule: commit the source change and the tracked dist/app.js together as one intent, use the primary-purpose type, and note in the body that the generated volume is required by the repo. Do not add dist/ to .gitignore.
